title: contoso.example
description: Parent domain used to resolve ForeignSecurityPrincipal mappings, recover trust-account material, and project access into enclave.example.

title: enclave.example
description: Restricted enclave reached through inter-realm ticketing and then extended through Enclave Access group placement and RBCD on an internal file server.

title: DUBLIN.contoso.example
description: Child domain where the main campaign runs: workstation foothold, local admin reuse, token theft, constrained delegation, SQL execution, and the first domain-controller compromise.

title: DUB-DC-1 ~ 10.200.2.1 (nwallace)
description: Dublin domain controller reached after privilege growth on the SQL host. This system marked the transition from host compromise to child-domain ownership and the bridge into the parent domain.

title: DUB-SQL-1 ~ 10.200.2.20 (iappleton > SYSTEM)
description: SQL Server in Dublin. Reached through constrained delegation and then converted into SQL CLR execution, a linked Beacon, SYSTEM, and the bridge toward the child-domain controller.

title: DUB-WEB-1 ~ 10.200.2.30 (tdobson)
description: Web-tier host in Dublin. This system exposed the constrained delegation relationship that made SQL access both practical and strategically important.

title: DUB-WKSTN-1 ~ 10.200.3.100 (administrator)
description: Secondary workstation reached through local-admin password reuse. Its main value was the tdobson token that opened the bridge into the web tier.

title: DUB-WKSTN-2 ~ 10.200.3.102 (consultant)
description: Initial foothold in Dublin. The first workstation provided the entry point, AppLocker-aware DLL execution, and the local-admin password reuse that started the chain.

title: ENC-FS-1 10.200.4.10 (SYSTEM)
description: Writing to the host as the ultimate goal

title: ENC-JMP-1 ~ 10.200.4.50 (SYSTEM)
description: Enclave jump host reached through inter-realm ticketing. This host exposed the ACLs that turned enclave access into enclave leverage through RBCD.

title: LON-DC-1 ~ 10.200.1.1 (SYSTEM)
description: Parent-domain controller used to resolve ForeignSecurityPrincipal mappings, identify the real Enclave Access relationship, and recover trust-account material for the enclave pivot.

title: Mitigation
description: Practical hardening ideas derived from the lab, covering local admin reuse, delegation, SQL execution paths, trust abuse, and enclave exposure.

title: MSSQL Execution Thread
description: How constrained delegation on DUB-WEB-1 became SQL administration, CLR-based execution, a linked Beacon, and then host-level control on DUB-SQL-1.

title: Workstation Compromise and Internal Pivot
description: Path 1 of the CRTO lab, from the first foothold on DUB-WKSTN-2 through local-admin password reuse and token theft into the Dublin web tier.

title: Constrained Delegation to SQL Compromise
description: Path 2 of the CRTO lab, where DUB-WEB-1 machine-account delegation becomes SQL sysadmin access, CLR execution, a linked Beacon, and control of DUB-SQL-1.

title: Child Domain to Root Domain Compromise
description: Path 3 of the CRTO lab, where control of DUB-SQL-1 becomes child-domain ownership on DUB-DC-1 and then administrative reach into the parent-domain controller LON-DC-1.

title: Trust Abuse and RBCD into ENCLAVE
description: Path 4 of the CRTO lab, where the parent-domain trust is abused to reach ENC-JMP-1 and then extended to ENC-FS-1 through RBCD.

title: Preparation of the C2
description: Defense and evasion notes for the CRTO lab, including the exact Malleable C2 choices used for staging, post-exploitation, and process injection.

title: gcbfinance.example

description: Enumerated from HR-ERIKA as hr\erika in the gcbhr.example domain.

title: gcbsec.example
description: Enumerated from SEC-SYSLOG01. No accessible trust relationship exists from IT, GCB, or GCBFINANCE — an intermediate pivot host was required for domain visibility.

description: Domain foothold y punto de entrada principal del environment.

title: msp.example
